slides.title: What does your mask protect you from?

body.text: This is scoring quick touches before a hug.

items: The touch player wins with three sets of two touches in a row.
The clinch player wins by closing his own hands around the touch player, under both elbows or chest to back.

body.text: This is passing the legs from on top.

items: The top player wins by touching both of the bottom player's knee pits with his own leg, feet off the mat.
The bottom player wins by making the top player sit down, then sitting up himself.

body.text: This is sitting on top of his belly.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps one of the bottom player's elbows covered.
The bottom player wins by touching both elbows to his body, or making the top player fall.

slides.title: What made it work?
slides.question: Tonight your guard kept people out while standing, passing, and pinning. What was it actually protecting?

options.feedback: A guard that protects something specific can be lowered on purpose. One that guards everything never comes down.
A habit with no reason behind it is hard to ever put down.

options.text: Whatever felt threatening at the time.
options.feedback: Guarding whatever feels threatening changes every day, and protects nothing in particular.
